notes: Source 4 = Magen 1989b, Qadmoniot (Hebrew); quotes are from the packet's English translation. The complex has two buildings: 'Building I is in the north, and Building II south of it' (p. 45). Building I is the main building. So the court cistern (s4f1) and the crypt L4, in the 'northern group of rooms' of Building I (s4f5, s4f6), are coded N relative to the site. s4f4: room L1 is in the NW corner of Building I. Its Hebrew name is 'breikhat shqi'a' (settling pool), but the source calls it small and it is a settling basin for gutter water, so pool_def is no. The court text's 'small settling basin' (p. 45) is probably the same basin. Not coded: the 'other cistern outside the building' that excess water was 'perhaps' led to (p. 47; conjectural); possible graves under room L8 (not established); drainage channels; sheep-folds. el-Qasr across the wadi (p. 50; map ref 1839/1490 = WBADB S1816) is described without any water or burial feature. No plan position: the plan has no coordinates and its north arrow is ambiguous. Late Roman pottery is mentioned (omitted in the packet) for an earlier phase, but no feature is dated by it, so the cistern stays U.
